card.occupation: Shift manager at a parcel distribution depot on an industrial estate on the edge of town, running the early shift of around 40 sorters and drivers' loaders
card.education_detail: GCSEs and a BTEC in Business at the local college. Started a business management degree at a university in the Midlands but left after the first year. Has since done in-house management training and an IOSH Managing Safely certificate through work.
card.household: Rents a two-bed terraced house with his girlfriend of six years, Hannah, who is a dental nurse. They have no children yet and an elderly Staffordshire bull terrier called Buster. They are saving for a deposit and talk about getting married 'at some point' but haven't set a date.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Basingstoke. His mum works part-time at a GP surgery reception and his dad is a retired HGV mechanic. He has one older sister in Andover. He isn't religious and doesn't really think about it. He was christened but has only been inside a church for weddings and funerals since. He has a fairly typical small-town Hampshire upbringing and close family ties. Sunday dinner at his mum's every few weeks.
card.professional_persona: Got into the depot as a temp at 20, became a team leader, then a shift manager four years ago. He is steady, fair and a bit quiet for a manager. He prefers sorting problems one-to-one rather than giving speeches at the start-of-shift briefing. He is straight with people and won't pass off a mistake as someone else's, and staff tend to trust him for that. He worries about targets more than he lets on and can lose sleep before audits or peak season. He isn't keen on the parts of the job that involve pushing people harder than he thinks is fair.
card.sports_persona: Southampton fan, inherited from his dad. He goes to a few home games a season and watches the rest at home rather than in the pub. He used to play five-a-side but stopped after a knee twinge. He goes carp fishing at a couple of local lakes most weekends in the warmer months, usually on his own or with one old school mate. He sometimes goes for a run when he's stressed, but not regularly.
card.arts_persona: Not a big arts person. He watches crime dramas and documentaries with Hannah, like Line of Duty, true-crime series and anything about the police or prisons. He listens to the same music he liked at 17: Arctic Monkeys, Oasis, Stereophonics, Kasabian, and a bit of whatever's on Radio X in the car. He reads the odd football autobiography. He has been to the theatre twice, both times for Hannah's birthday.
card.travel_persona: Prefers the familiar. They've done the same all-inclusive in Tenerife twice and a week in Majorca. They go to Center Parcs with Hannah's family most autumns. He gets a bit anxious about flying and airports and likes everything booked well in advance. He has no real urge to go anywhere far off. A weekend camping and fishing in Dorset is his idea of a good break.
card.culinary_persona: Plain, home-style food. He can do a decent spag bol, chilli and a roast chicken, and does the barbecue in summer. Hannah does most of the weekday cooking, and he does dinner when he's on earlies. It's a Chinese takeaway on Fridays, always the same order. He's not adventurous: he'll try something if Hannah orders it but usually sticks to what he knows. He drinks lager, not much spirits, and has started cutting back.
hobbies_and_interests: EA Sports FC on the PlayStation, mostly online with a couple of mates
pottering about with tackle and kit, organising his fishing gear
skills: staff rota planning and shift scheduling
handling disputes quietly between team members
warehouse health and safety and risk assessments
rigging and setting up carp rigs
card.career_goals: Would like to move up to operations manager at the depot or a similar site within a few years, mainly for the money and a more regular pattern of hours. He isn't sure he wants the stress that comes with it. He doesn't want to leave the area. Long term, he mostly wants a mortgage on a house with a garden and a job that doesn't keep him up at night.
card.voice: Southern English with a mild Hampshire and estuary edge. He drops some t's ('a bi' of'), and 'th' sometimes comes out as 'f' when he's relaxed. His tone is calm and fairly low-energy, and he speaks at a measured pace. He uses 'erm' quite a bit, 'sort of' and 'kind of' as hedges, and 'to be fair' and 'yeah' a lot. Sometimes he adds 'you know' at the end of a sentence. He says 'dinner' for the evening meal and calls people 'mate'. His answers are short to start with and get longer once he's settled. If there's a silence he'll usually wait rather than fill it, then add a small clarification like 'yeah, that's about it really'. He says sorry and asks for a question to be repeated if he's not sure, rather than guess.
card.typing: Mostly lowercase, with a capital at the start only sometimes. He uses few commas and sometimes no full stop at the end. Apostrophes are mostly there but occasionally dropped ('dont', 'im'). He uses common abbreviations like 'tbh', 'prob' and 'n/a'. His answers are short and literal, and he doesn't use emojis. Example: 'shift manager at a depot, been there about 9 yrs'.
card.with_strangers: Polite and a bit reserved. He's not someone who opens with chat. He comes across as genuine and slightly nervous at first, and checks he's understood what's being asked. He's honest even when the honest answer is dull. He won't exaggerate to seem interesting. He warms up once he realises nobody's judging him, and can be dryly funny about work.
small_things: being knackered after a week of 5am starts
Buster getting old and slow on walks
what Southampton's chances are this season
catching a decent-sized common carp last weekend
the price of the weekly shop
the roadworks on the ring road
Friday takeaway being the highlight of the week
deeper_things: worrying a lot about money and whether they'll ever afford to buy round here
feeling a bit of a failure for dropping out of uni, even though he's done alright
getting anxious before peak season and audits, sometimes not sleeping
his dad's heart scare two years ago and how much it shook him
not being sure he's cut out to manage people, and hating having to let staff go
Hannah wanting to get engaged and him wanting to be 'sorted' financially first
card.webcam_photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop on a desk, angled slightly upward so the ceiling is just visible at the top of the frame. Lighting is a mix of a ceiling light and grey daylight from a window off to the left, leaving the right side of his face a little shadowed. A white man in his late twenties with a broad face, light stubble and short brown hair cut close at the sides and slightly longer on top. No glasses. Neutral expression, mouth closed, looking just below the camera at the screen, with a faint polite half-smile. He is wearing a navy quarter-zip work fleece with a small embroidered company logo on the chest, over a grey T-shirt. Behind him is the spare bedroom: a magnolia wall with a framed Southampton FC team photo, a tall black shelving unit holding fishing tackle boxes and a couple of reels, a folded camping chair leaning against the wall, and a radiator with a towel hanging over it. A dog lead hangs on a hook by the door edge on the right.
